title: feat(app-shell): the AI usage indicator renders the reset line for the 5-hour pace window (objectui#11415)
body:
Fixes #11415
Clause-②: no

## What changes

`AiUsageIndicator` renders the reset line for `resetKind: 'fiveHour'`. That is the rolling 5-hour pace window from cloud#2059, which cloud#2574 puts on `GET /api/v1/ai/usage`. Before this PR a `fiveHour` pool fell through to the unknown-kind path, so a user stopped by the pace limit saw no line telling them when they could continue.

- `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useAiUsage.ts`: `AiUsageResetKind` gains `'fiveHour'`. The `daily` / `monthly` members stay: production cloud `v1.33.0` still emits them, per triage `5943548946`. The `resetsAt` doc comment now names both rolling windows.
- `packages/app-shell/src/layout/AiUsageIndicator.tsx`: `resetLabel` gains a `fiveHour` arm. It reads "Resets in N hours", counted down from `resetsAt` and the measured `now` only, like the weekly arm. The hours count lives in one helper, `hoursResetLabel`, which the weekly arm's final day now also calls. The weekly output is unchanged: same rounding, same key, and its existing tests still pass. There is no line while `resetsAt` is `null` or `now` is not measured yet, and an unknown `resetKind` still renders no line (objectui#7371's soft-fail; its pin with `'quarterly'` is untouched).
- No locale pack changes (see the key-family decision below).
- `.changeset/11415-ai-usage-five-hour-reset.md`: `@object-ui/app-shell` patch.
- Out of scope, untouched: the cloud side, the `topUp` CTA, and removing `daily` / `monthly`. Triage says that removal waits for a cloud release that carries cloud#2574.

## Decisions this PR takes

### Key family: reuse `console.ai.usage.resetsWeeklyHours`, no new family

The PM's hypothesis 2 held. I read the hours family's text in all ten packs, and none of them names a window:

| pack | `resetsWeeklyHours_other` |
|---|---|
| en | Resets in {{count}} hours |
| de | Wird in {{count}} Stunden zurückgesetzt |
| es | Se restablece en {{count}} horas |
| fr | Réinitialisation dans {{count}} heures |
| pt | Redefine em {{count}} horas |
| ru | Сброс через {{count}} часов |
| ja | {{count}}時間後にリセットされます |
| ko | {{count}}시간 후 초기화됩니다 |
| zh | {{count}} 小时后重置 |
| ar | {{count}} ساعات حتى إعادة التعيين |

The `_one` and base keys follow the same pattern. A new family would duplicate these strings in all ten packs (and ship `@object-ui/i18n`) without changing anything a user reads. The cost is that the key name says "Weekly" while it now serves two windows. The comment above `hoursResetLabel` says why the copy is shared, so if someone later edits the weekly copy to mention the week, the cost is visible at the call site.

### Under one hour: round up to 1 hour, no minutes arm

The card leaves this to the implementer. The four axes:

- **Real business need.** The line is for the user who has hit the 5-hour wall. Rounding up means the line never promises a reset earlier than the real one, so a user who waits as told never hits the wall again. A minutes reading would be more precise only in the last hour of a window. Nobody measured any demand for it, and the card accepts rounding up.
- **Long-term soundness.** It is one rounding rule for both rolling windows (the weekly arm already rounds up and clamps to 1). It is still derived only from `resetsAt`. A minutes arm would also make the 60-second `now` tick visible in the text, which the component's comment rules out today ("the countdown is day/hour-grained").
- **Preventing AI mistakes.** No metadata or contract is involved, so this axis is neutral. Fewer key families also means fewer chances to break a pack.
- **Startup focus.** A minutes arm needs a new plural family in ten packs, with nine translations nobody reviewed, for a speculative gain. The default here is to stay tight, so no minutes arm.

Recommendation, and what this PR does: round up and clamp to 1. A reset 10 minutes away reads "Resets in 1 hour", never "0 hours".

## Tests

All runs below are at head `8ea5c871` unless marked otherwise. Node `v22.22.2` from `/opt/nvm/versions/node`, because the container's `v22.22.0` is refused by this repo's engine-strict install.

- **Red first** (the new tests on the unchanged source, before the fix commit): `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/layout/__tests__/AiUsageIndicator.test.tsx`: `Tests  3 failed | 17 passed (20)`. The three failures were the `fiveHour` 3-hours, under-an-hour and real-hook cases. The `resetsAt: null` case passed, because the old code renders no line for any `fiveHour` pool.
- **Green**: `pnpm exec vitest run` over every suite that imports `useAiUsage` / `AiUsageIndicator`. The suite list came from `git grep -l -E 'useAiUsage|AiUsageIndicator' -- '*.test.ts' '*.test.tsx'`: `useAiUsage.test.ts`, `AiUsageIndicator.test.tsx`, the three `ChatDock*` suites and `scripts/__tests__/check-vi-mock-specifiers.test.ts`. Result: `Test Files  6 passed (6)`, `Tests  90 passed (90)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0. Run after building the dependency closure with `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build` (29 packages, exit 0). `--listFilesOnly` confirms that the test project compiles `AiUsageIndicator.test.tsx`, so the new test's `resetKind: 'fiveHour'` literals are type-checked against the widened union.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell build`: exit 0. `dist completeness: 1 package(s) complete`, and `fiveHour` appears in the emitted `dist/layout/AiUsageIndicator.js` and `dist/hooks/useAiUsage.d.ts`.
- Gates, all exit 0: `pnpm check:i18n-keys`, `pnpm check:control-bytes`, `pnpm check:new-line-citations` (`0 new citation(s)`), `pnpm changeset:check`, `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` (`3 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)`), `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit`, and the test-file gates `check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `check-test-path-roots`, `check-vi-mock-specifiers` and `check-vi-mock-inherit`. `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the four paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- **ESLint, narrowed to the three touched source files**, with the three pieces of evidence the narrowing needs. (1) The population is the root `eslint.config.js` that app-shell's `lint` script (`eslint .`) reads, and the test file is not in its ignores (`--print-config` exit 0). (2) `--format json` reports 3 files linted, 0 errors and 2 warnings. Both warnings are `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` on effect bodies this PR does not touch, and linting the base versions of the same files through stdin gives the same 2 warnings. (3) The config is not type-aware (no `parserOptions` / `projectService` in `eslint.config.js`), and the repo's custom rules read no other files, so this diff cannot change a verdict on any file it does not touch. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.
- No i18n test was run: no locale pack changed.

## Acceptance notes

- **ru plural forms on the hours family (pre-existing, same class as objectui#10024 and objectui#3863).** The packs carry two slots (`_one` / `_other` plus a base key), and `ru` falls back to the base key at 2 to 4. A probe of the shipped `ru` pack with plain i18next printed `Сброс через 2 часов`, `3 часов` and `4 часов`; Russian needs `часа` there. The weekly arm's final day already shows this. The `fiveHour` arm makes counts 2 to 4 routine, since three of its five possible readings fall there. It is not repaired here: the locale packs are outside this card's file surface. Reported to the seat to fold into that family.
- **An unparseable `resetsAt` renders `NaN`.** `isPool` checks `resetsAt` only as a string, so a non-ISO value would render "Resets in NaN hours" (or "NaN days" on the weekly arm). This is pre-existing and no named producer emits such a value. The contract-first place to refuse it is the parser, not the label.
- **Key-name drift.** `resetsWeeklyHours` now serves the weekly final day and the 5-hour window (decision above). Nobody is currently set to rename it.

## Overlap

The claim's serial-constraint read found no open PR touching `AiUsage*`, `useAiUsage` or `packages/i18n/src/locales`. `main` was merged at `f88a900e` before this PR was opened.
